title: Factory policy: every delivery-loop rule value decided once, on the server

story.as_a: session or hook enforcing a delivery-loop rule
story.i_want_to: read the rule's value from loopctl's one factory policy
story.so_that: a rule changes in one place and the prose, the hooks and the server can never state two different values

rationale: PRD section 3, concept 4: every rule is decided once, on the server; hooks and prose are generated from that policy or are thin calls to it. Today one value lives in several places with nothing checking they agree: the review ceilings are in claude-config CLAUDE.md:54 and in review-round-counter (README.md:9-12, hooks.ts), the PR-body sections in CLAUDE.md:50 and in gate-pr-body.sh via bin/pr-body-sections.sh, the epic-merge tip age in gate-epic-merge-green-base.sh:141. This story makes factory/policy.toml the one source, compiled into the server and served to every client.

acceptance_criteria.description: Loopctl.Factory.Policy reads factory/policy.toml at compile time (@external_resource) and the build fails, naming the key path, when the file has an unknown key, a missing required key or a value of the wrong type.
Loopctl.Factory.Policy.get/0 returns %Policy{schema: 1, version: v, rules: map} where v is the lowercase hex sha256 of the policy file's bytes.
Loopctl.Factory.Policy.fetch!/1 takes a dotted path ("review_rounds.code.ceiling") and returns its value, or raises Loopctl.Factory.Policy.UnknownRule naming the path.

The shipped policy.toml holds today's values: review_rounds prose normal 1 ceiling 2, code normal 2 ceiling 3; open_prs_per_session 2; epics_open_per_repo 3; pr_body.required_sections ["Testing", "Risk", "How to revert"]; review.default_level "medium" and review.max_level "high"; epic_merge.new_tip_seconds 600; protected_branches ["master", "main"].

GET /api/v1/factory/policy, behind RequireRole role: :agent, answers 200 {schema, version, rules} with an ETag header equal to the version, and 304 with no body when If-None-Match carries that version.
The policy is product, not tenant data: keys of two different tenants receive the same version and rules, and a request with no valid key is answered 401.

The MCP tool factory_policy calls GET /api/v1/factory/policy, says in its description that it needs any tenant key and refuses nothing else, and is pinned by a wiring test and a row in mcp-server/README.md.

technical_notes: Why a new module and route: Loopctl.DeliveryGates.Triggers (lib/loopctl/delivery_gates/triggers.ex:1-30) is the Gate B path document, operator-pinned by sha256 and kept out of source on purpose ('the list is a map of which paths skip human review'), with a closed per-repo schema (@repo_keys at :37); delivery-loop rules are reviewed product behaviour that must ship with the release set, so they cannot live there. Loopctl.SystemConfig (lib/loopctl/system_config.ex:1-25) holds live-tunable integer knobs with a node-local cache whose cross-node refresh is unbounded during a netsplit or rolling deploy, so a hook and a node could read two values; the policy must equal the generated pack exactly, which only a compiled file gives.
Gate B's independent_paths (renamed from human_paths in release 2, US-52.12) stays in Triggers: it is per-repo operator data, not a fleet rule.

Value sources this story copies, so the shipped file starts equal to today: review ceilings /home/mkreyman/workspace/claude-config/plugins/review-round-counter/README.md:9-12 and CLAUDE.md:54; two open PRs CLAUDE.md:46; three epics CLAUDE.md:58; PR-body sections CLAUDE.md:50; review levels CLAUDE.md:51; tip age hooks/gate-epic-merge-green-base.sh:141 (EPIC_MERGE_NEW_TIP_SECONDS, default 600).

At the review-round ceiling the session decides whether to dispatch a redesign or narrow what merges; nothing waits and nothing messages Mark (PRD R2; Mark, 2026-11-19: 'let the loop decid[e]'). So the policy has no pause key: the ceilings are its only review-round values, and the REVIEW CAP pause of claude-config CLAUDE.md:54 and hooks/lib/review-cap.sh is not carried over (factory/inventory.toml records it retired).

Route: add get "/factory/policy" to the agent-role /api/v1 scope beside get "/chg_ledger/summary" (lib/loopctl_web/router.ex:550); release 5 adds /factory/overview in the same scope (README names table: visibility). Controller pattern: ChgLedgerSummaryController (lib/loopctl_web/controllers/chg_ledger_summary_controller.ex:30, plug LoopctlWeb.Plugs.RequireRole, [role: :agent]). operation/2 lists 200, 304, 401.
lib/loopctl/factory/policy.ex; the TOML parser is the one US-52.50 uses. schema is an integer bumped on any key rename or removal; clients accept their own schema and the previous one (PRD R7).

MCP: mcp-server/lib/factory-policy.js, declaration and case in mcp-server/index.js, row in the 'Runner and delivery-loop tools' table of mcp-server/README.md (:522); the route_coverage sweep (mcp-server/test/route_coverage.test.js) then finds the route covered.
CHANGELOG.md: a new public route, operator-facing (CLAUDE.md, Doc hygiene).
non_goals: Generating hooks and prose from the policy: US-52.52.
Counting review rounds on the server: US-52.53.
Per-repo overrides of a rule (the .chg/policy.toml [review] map keeps its role in chg).

failure_modes.partition: AC-52.51.5: a client that cannot reach loopctl keeps the policy.json the pack shipped with (US-52.52); the ETag lets it confirm on reconnect that nothing changed without re-reading the body.
failure_modes.state: AC-52.51.1: the policy lives in factory/policy.toml under version control and is compiled into the release, so every node of one release serves the same bytes and a restart loses nothing.
failure_modes.retry: AC-52.51.5: the route is a read; a retried GET returns the same version or a 304.
failure_modes.slow: AC-52.51.5: the 304 path sends no body, so a slow client re-checks with one small response.
failure_modes.reach: n/a: the policy is compiled into each node and served inline in the request process; nothing is queued.

defaults: Every value in AC-52.51.4 is today's value from claude-config (owner may change any in factory/policy.toml).
The route is open to any tenant key at role agent; it carries no tenant data.
definition_of_done: From an MCP session: factory_policy returns rules.review_rounds.code.ceiling = 3 and a version equal to sha256sum factory/policy.toml on the deployed commit.
